If you follow [R-loggers](https://www.r-bloggers.com/) you will probably know that I have been publishing my selection of the "Top 40" new R packages on CRAN for quite some time. First as part of my work at Revolution Analytics, then on [R Views](https://rviews.rstudio.com/) for RStudio and Posit, and now on here on R Works. It used to take about a day's worth of pleasurable work spread out over a month. For a hundred or so packages I could look at all of the package webpages, download and and play with a small number of them. Now the "Top 40" has become a real hamster on the wheel project. The following plot shows my count of the number of new packages to stick to CRAN since I started R Works. (Stick to CRAN means I try to account for the small number of packages that are accepted by CRAN during the a month but are subsequently removed before the middle of the next month.)


```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show plot code"
library(tidyverse)
file_path <- "new-cran-pkgs.csv"

if (!file.exists(file_path)) {
  stop(paste("File not found! Please check the path:", file_path))
}

# Read text and numbers safely
raw_data <- read.csv(file_path, colClasses = c("character", "numeric"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

plot_data <- raw_data |> mutate(Date = my(Month)) |>
  arrange(Date)

new_pkg <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Date, y = Num_pkgs, group = 1)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1f77b4", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#d62728", size = 1.2) +

  labs(
    title = "Monthly Volume of New CRAN Packages",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Number of Packages",
    caption = "Source: R Works monthly Top 40 posts"
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

new_pkg
```

What could possibly be going on? Well, I have a guess. But, the real question are most of these new packages a real contribution the the R Community, or are they part of an apparently general software trend identified by John Burn-Murdoch writing in the Financial Times.
